articles.title: Rise in Cash-Pay GLP-1s Alters Employer Benefit Utilization Trends
articles.summary: An increasing number of patients are bypassing traditional insurance and paying out-of-pocket for GLP-1 medications due to strict prior authorization and coverage exclusions by employers. This trend shifts utilization patterns outside employer-sponsored health plans, potentially impacting overall cost management strategies and employee satisfaction. Self-funded plan sponsors must evaluate whether cash-pay trends signal a need to redesign their obesity and diabetes benefit offerings.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Economics; Mon, 05 Oct 2026 18:07:30 GMT

articles.title: Bipartisan Congressional Scrutiny Intensifies Against Pharmacy Benefit Managers
articles.summary: Lawmakers from both major political parties are increasingly targeting pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) for legislative reform, focusing on pricing practices and transparency. This bipartisan momentum signals potential federal policy changes that will impact how PBMs operate and report costs to self-funded employers. Self-funded health plan sponsors should monitor these developments as they may yield new transparency mandates and regulatory compliance requirements.

articles.title: SHARx Warns Self-Funded Employers That Discounts Fail to Control Total Pharmacy Spending
articles.summary: Industry analysis highlights that relying solely on traditional pharmaceutical discounts is insufficient for self-funded employers managing escalating pharmacy costs. The report emphasizes the need for comprehensive cost-management strategies beyond standard rebate models to address the total cost of care. This directly impacts employer benefits planning and PBM evaluation criteria.
articles.source_line: Source: PR Newswire; Mon, 05 Oct 2026 12:08:00 GMT
